<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard AUR git package for the studyplan application. It fetches source from the upstream GitHub repository via `git+$url.git`, which is expected behavior for -git packages. The `sha256sums` are set to `SKIP`, which is required and ordinary for VCS sources. The `pkgver()` function computes version information from Cargo.toml and git metadata - a common pattern. The `prepare()` step runs `cargo fetch --locked` to retrieve dependencies from the official Rust registry, and `build()`/`check()` invoke standard `cargo build` and `cargo test` commands. The `package()` function installs the compiled binary and documentation to standard locations using `install`. No network downloads from unexpected hosts, no obfuscated code, no eval/base64 chains, and no data exfiltration or backdoor mechanisms are present. All operations align with routine AUR packaging practices for a Rust application.

The only notable aspect is the unpinned VCS source (`git+$url.git` without a specific commit), but this is explicitly noted as normal for -git packages and not a security concern on its own.
</details>
